Every listed set must be a clique with at least two vertices and every edge must lie in exactly one listed clique. Minimize the total number of cliques. The score totals clique partition sizes on two fixed dense graphs; it measures a partitioning method.

sources.locator: Paul Erdős, A. W. Goodman and Louis Pósa, The Representation of a Graph by Set Intersections (1966). Crossref records inspected (Erdős, Goodman and Pósa 1966; Győri and Keszegh 2017). Erdős Problem #1017 page inspected: every graph has an edge partition into at most n^2/4 edges and triangles; Erdős asked for sharpening when there are more than n^2/4 edges; Győri and Keszegh settled the K4-free case. The score totals clique partition sizes on two fixed dense graphs; it measures a partitioning method.

name: Colouring four fixed planar bipartite graphs from lists of three colours
description: construct() -> four colourings, one per instance from planar_bipartite_lists(splits, seed) for (20,701), (40,702), (60,703), (100,704) in the verifier: a bipartite quadrangulation grown from the cube by inserting squares into random faces (minimum degree 3), with a random list of 3 colours from 0..4 per vertex. Each vertex must take a colour from its list and adjacent vertices must differ. The score is the number of properly coloured instances (0..4). Maximize; all are colourable by the Alon-Tarsi theorem. The score counts fixed instances coloured properly from their lists; it measures a constructive list-colouring method for a theorem proved non-constructively.

sources.locator: Noga Alon and Michael Tarsi, Colorings and orientations of graphs (1992). Crossref record and abstract inspected: Alon and Tarsi's orientation theorem (a graph with an orientation of maximum outdegree d whose even and odd Eulerian subgraphs differ in number is (d+1)-choosable) implies that every planar bipartite graph is 3-choosable. No Erdős Problems page corresponds to this bank entry. The score counts fixed instances coloured properly from their lists; it measures a constructive list-colouring method for a theorem proved non-constructively.

name: Large sum-free subsets of three fixed sets of integers
description: construct() -> three subsets, one per instance from sum_free_instance(size, seed) for (60,801), (120,802), (240,803) in the verifier (distinct nonzero integers in [-10000, 10000]). Each subset must be sum-free: no a + b = c with a, b, c in it (a = b allowed). Maximize the total size; every n-element set has a sum-free subset of size at least (n+2)/3 (Bourgain). The score totals sum-free subset sizes on three fixed random sets; it measures a search method, not the worst case in f(n).

sources.locator: Sean Eberhard, Ben Green and Freddie Manners, Sets of integers with no large sum-free subset (2014). Crossref record inspected; Erdős Problem #792 page inspected (f(n) >= n/3 (Erdős), (n+2)/3 (Bourgain), n/3 + c log log n (Bedert 2025); f(n) <= n/3 + o(n) (Eberhard, Green and Manners); Problem 1 on Green's list). The score totals sum-free subset sizes on three fixed random sets; it measures a search method, not the worst case in f(n).
